newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MONTREAL EXPLODES FOR 17 HITS AND SIX HOMERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MONTREAL EXPLODES FOR 17 HITS AND SIX HOMERS.

text.p: Even the pitcher got into the act as the Montreal Expos exploded for 17 hits, including six home runs, in a 9-3 thumping of the San Diego Padres on Sunday.
Starting pitcher Jim Bullinger homered and carried a one-hitter into the ninth inning and Rondell White went 4-for-5 with two homers and four RBI to pace the Expos' offensive eruption.
Vladimir Guerrero, Henry Rodriguez and Chris Widger also homered for the Expos.

Bullinger (2-4) gave up one hit over 8 1/3 innings before serving up back-to-back homers to Ken Caminiti and Chris Jones in the ninth. He retired 13 straight batters from the fourth through the eighth inning.
Sterling Hitchcock (2-3) surrendered five runs, including four homers, in 4 1/3 innings to get the loss.
"Today was just an all-around bad day for us," Padres manager Bruce Bochy said.
The Padres scored the first run of the game in the second inning on Chris Gomez's RBI double, but the Expos scored the next nine runs to put it away.

At Colorado, Roger Bailey became the first pitcher in the majors to record two shutouts this season as the Rockies cruised to a 9-0 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies, giving manager Don Baylor his 300th career win.
Bailey (4-1) scattered nine hits and stayed out of trouble by not walking a batter to become the first Colorado pitcher to notch a pair of shutouts in the same season.
Larry Walker had three hits and four RBI and Eric Young and Andres Galarraga also had three hits apiece for the Rockies, who won for the 10th time in their last 13 games.
In Atlanta, Terrell Wade won for the first time this season as the Braves used a two-run error for a 3-1 victory that salvaged the finale of a three-game series with the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Wade (1-1) gave up six hits in five-plus innings before leaving after allowing a sixth-inning run. Relievers Paul Byrd, Mike Bielecki and Mark Wohlers shut down the Pirates the rest of the way.
Atlanta scored three runs in the third off Francisco Cordova -- one on an RBI single by Chipper Jones and two when right fielder Emil Brown dropped a Ryan Klesko fly ball.
In San Francisco, Glenallen Hill delivered a two-out bases-loaded single in the bottom of the 10th inning to lift the Giants to a 2-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
The Reds broke a scoreless tie in the top of the 10th when Deion Sanders scored as Bill Mueller let Barry Larkin's grounder go through his legs at third base.

The Giants loaded the bases in the bottom of the 10th as Marvin Benard walked, Mueller was hit by a pitch and Barry Bonds walked. Hill's bloop of the first pitch he saw from Jeff Brantley dropped in front of right fielder Lenny Harris to bring home Benard and pinch-runner Dante Powell.
In New York, Todd Stottlemyre allowed three hits over eight strong innings and Willie McGee and Ray Lankford belted two-run homers to lead the St Louis Cardinals to a 8-2 thumping of the Mets.
Stottlemyre (1-1) allowed two runs and three walks, striking out five for the win.

Mets starter Mark Clark (3-2) saw his personal three-game winning streak snapped, getting tagged for six runs and eight hits in four innings. He surrendered both homers in his shortest outing of the season.
In Los Angeles, Chan Ho Park allowed five hits over 6 2/3 innings and Mike Piazza added a long solo homer as the Dodgers beat the Chicago Cubs 5-2.
Park (2-1) continued his impressive season by allowing two runs and three walks, striking out five. In his last 29 1/3 innings, Park has 21 strike outs.
Piazza's sixth homer in the fourth inning against Cubs starter Steve Trachsel (1-4) gave the Dodgers a 3-0 lead. Todd Zeile's RBI single later in the inning made it 4-0.
In Houston, Darryl Kile pitched a four-hitter for his first shutout in nearly four years to outduel Kevin Brown and give the Astros a 1-0 victory over the Florida Marlins.

Kile (2-2), who gave up one hit over the final six innings, walked three and struck out six for his first shutout since August 17, 1993. Brown (3-2) was nearly as tough, allowing five hits and no walks while striking out 10.
The only run Brown allowed was in the first inning when Jeff Bagwell scored from second on Luis Gonzalez's single to left field.
